official.deadline_central_display: March 1 (BI states the date without a year)
official.deadline_note: BI publishes only 'Application deadline is March 1'. For the current admission cycle, with a master's start in the following autumn, that falls on 1 March 2027. BI also states that all scholarship decisions are finalized by the end of April and cannot be appealed.
official.application_cycle: Autumn intake following the 1 March application deadline
official.status_note: BI's page, updated 6 October 2026, presents the scholarship as an ongoing entrance award for admission to a full-time master's programme, with a 1 March application deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: The award covers full tuition fees for up to two years of study at master's level; a separate stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester supports living expenses if the student meets progress requirements.
benefits: Full tuition fees covered for up to two years of full-time study in a master's degree programme at BI
A stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, conditional on meeting academic progression requirements
Recipients are also considered for the BI Presidential Scholarship, the Master International Scholarship and the Women in Finance and Tech Scholarship
Scholarship holders are recognised as BI Ambassadors and support student recruitment and events
eligibility: Citizenship of an African nation, and not a resident of Norway or a domestic applicant on the basis of educational background
Seeking a first graduate or master's degree; only applicants for their first master's degree are considered
Admission to the first year of a full-time master's degree programme at BI's Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim campus

Preference is given to candidates with African citizenship who are currently enrolled at or recently graduated from a GBSN member school in Africa, or who have participated in a GMAC Study in Europe event in Africa, or who have been awarded a certificate of participation in a SEED Business School Festival event in Africa
requirements: A strong GMAT or GRE score; BI says an accepted applicant needs this average of results, and it is verified with your official test result
A minimum overall GPA 4.0 on a scale up to 5.0, as awarded by your university (or other outside institution), in your Bachelor's qualification. International grades are converted by BI

Academic progression requirements to keep the stipend: full study progression at both the first and second semester (normally 30 ECTS each) with at least the stipulated progression requirements in the study programme, a cumulative BI-equivalent GPA of 'B' or better on the BI ECTS scale, and no failing grades
Documentation submitted at the time of application is the only documentation considered, including grades and test results; late or supplementary documentation is not added
Applications must be submitted through the online application portal, not by email
documents: Online application for the master's programme plus scholarship application letter of maximum one page uploaded to the 'Scholarship' section of the application portal
CV or resume uploaded to the 'Scholarship' section of the application portal

Identification within the application letter of the GBSN membership of your African school or the GMAC or SEED Business School Festival event taken part in, with the date and country or place in Africa
Transcript and diploma evidence of the required GPA
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded based on academic merit at BI, not financial need
Award value may differ from year to year depending on funds available
The majority of scholarship decisions are communicated near the end of April, and all applicants are informed of the outcome by the end of April
coverage: Full tuition fees for up to two years of study at master's level
Living-expense stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester
Travel and insurance costs are not covered
application_method: Apply for admission to a full-time master's programme at BI through the online application portal at the same time as the scholarship application
Upload your CV or resume and a scholarship application letter of maximum one page to the 'Scholarship' section
State the GBSN, GMAC or SEED link with date and country in the application letter
Register for and report a strong GMAT or GRE score as part of the same application
official.application_route: Apply through BI's online application portal for the master's programme and the scholarship simultaneously; scholarship materials are uploaded to the 'Scholarship' section of the portal and email applications are not considered.
official.citizenship_residency: Citizenship of an African nation; applicants who are residents of Norway or are considered domestic applicants on the basis of educational background are not eligible.
official.international_eligibility: This is an international award aimed at African nationals who are not Norway-based: the only entry route is as an international applicant, and applicants who are domestic by educational background are excluded.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to all full-time master's programmes at BI (Master of Science programmes in Business, Business Analytics, Finance, Marketing, Strategy, Sustainable Finance, Accounting, Economics, International Management and similar), excluding the BI-Luiss Joint European Master in Marketing (JEMM), which is explicitly out of scope.
official.duration: Full tuition covered for up to two years of master's study, with the living-expense stipend paid per semester
official.description: BI is a member of the Global Business School Network (GBSN) and participates in the GMAC Study in Europe Initiative and the SEED Business School Festival in Africa, and therefore offers two $20,000 Equivalency Approved scholarships to support these initiatives, specifically in Africa. The Future African Leader Scholarship, which covers full tuition for up to two years of study in a full-time master's degree and a stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester for living expenses, is intended to build a network of talented African leaders with knowledge of Norwegian business, technology and sustainability.
official.program_type: Business school entrance scholarship for master's study in Norway

not_confirmed: Deadline year: BI publishes 'Application deadline is March 1' without a year, so 1 March 2027 is an inference for the next cycle rather than a stated date
English_requirement: BI does not publish an English requirement on this page; language requirements sit on the individual programme admission pages

The reciprocal-equivalency scholarship total is quoted on the page as '$20,000 Equivalency' for the GBSN-linked award, while the award value covered here is stated in Norwegian kroner; the two figures are presented differently on BI's own page
Number of scholarships offered is stated as two, against the four awards offered across the three initiatives in total, so the allocation to this specific scholarship is not itemised
verification.notes: Read directly from BI Norwegian Business School's own Future African Leader Scholarship page (last updated 6 October 2026, and verified on 10 October 2026). Two things on the page are worth flagging: the campus list now includes Trondheim alongside Oslo and Bergen, and the SEED Business School Festival has been added to the GBSN and GMAC participation routes. Note also the page's own description of the reciprocal scholarships' value is a summary block that is not entirely consistent with the stated NOK amounts.

applicant_utility.summary: This is one of two awards BI offers to African nationals, and it is effectively a tuition-free master's plus a per-semester stipend, so it removes the largest single cost for an African student studying in Oslo, Bergen or Trondheim. The competitive filter is academic: you need both a strong GMAT or GRE and a minimum overall GPA of 4.0 out of 5.0, and BI converts international grades itself so you should not translate your transcript yourself. Importantly, you apply for the programme and the scholarship in the same submission, and everything you want BI to consider must already be attached at that moment, because BI states that deadlines, scholarship amounts and coverage are not negotiable. Award decisions are announced by the end of April and cannot be appealed.
applicant_utility.best_fit: An African national with a strong first degree and a competitive GMAT or GRE who wants a fully tuition-covered MSc in business or related fields at a Norwegian business school and can clear the GPA threshold.
application_readiness_checklist: Book the GMAT or GRE early enough to have an official score before you submit, because BI verifies the score
Check your university's grading scale: the minimum overall GPA of 4.0 out of 5.0 is what BI applies, and international grades are converted by BI
Identify your GBSN member school in Africa, or the GMAC Study in Europe or SEED Business School Festival event you attended, with its date and country, and put this in the application letter
Prepare the CV or resume and a one-page scholarship application letter for upload to the 'Scholarship' section of the portal
Confirm the master's programme you want is not the BI-Luiss Joint European Master
Submit the programme admission and scholarship application together through the portal; do not wait to be admitted first
common_rejection_risks: Sending an email application instead of using the portal: email applications are not considered
Missing the GPA threshold, or assuming BI will accept a different scale conversion: BI converts grades itself
Leaving out the GBSN, GMAC or SEED link with date and country, which is how preference is established
Applying for the excluded BI-Luiss Joint European Master programme
Expecting to appeal: BI states that deadlines, amounts and coverage are not up for negotiation and all applicants are informed by end of April
Expecting the stipend without meeting progression requirements: full study progression and a cumulative 'B' average are conditions of the stipend
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel, insurance, health cover and personal costs: the award covers tuition and pays a stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester, but travel and insurance are explicitly not included.
document_audit: Only documentation submitted at the time of application is considered, including grades and test results: there is no chance to add documents later
The diploma and transcript from your bachelor's institution must be available to upload at application time, not after admission
alerts: BI states it is currently reviewing improvements to its scholarship offers, so amounts may change

The same scholarship page's own summary block describes the two reciprocal-equivalency figures in rather cumbersome language and mixes currencies and totals; treat the NOK amounts as the operative figures and confirm with the admissions team if you are budgeting
Recipients are expected to support BI's student recruitment and events as BI Ambassadors
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply online through BI's application portal for the chosen master's programme, uploading the scholarship application letter, CV or resume, and the supporting documentation to the 'Scholarship' section of the same application.
